BiblicalUsage: Mits is pressure — the squeezing that brings something out. The proverb stacks three pictures: churning milk brings butter, wringing a nose brings blood, and forcing wrath brings strife.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe pressure always produces something, so I watch what I am pressing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
